title: Enzyme inhibition and metabolic control; Membrane structure (fluid mosaic)
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for OCR A-level (A) Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: MB01a#t1 term and clue written for the game; MB01a#t2 term and clue written for the game; EZ03#t2 term and clue written for the game; MB01a#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: EZ03#N.2, MB01a#N.3a, EZ03#N.11, MB01a#N.7, EZ03#N.14, MB01a#N.10a.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Phospholipid
items.clue: Molecule with a charged, water-loving head and two non-polar fatty acid tails.

items.label: Hydrophobic
items.clue: Describes non-polar parts, such as fatty acid tails, that are kept away from water.

items.label: Active site
items.clue: Where the substrate normally binds; a molecule of similar shape can occupy it instead.

items.label: Integral protein
items.clue: Membrane component embedded in one or both layers, sometimes spanning the whole bilayer.

questions.stem: In a hypothetical bacterium, compound S is made from compound P by a pathway of three enzyme-catalysed steps: P → Q → R → S. Enzyme 1 converts P to Q, enzyme 2 converts Q to R, and enzyme 3 converts R to S. A mutation makes enzyme 2 non-functional. Which prediction about the mutant bacterium is best supported?

options.text: Only R is affected; Q and S are still made at their usual rates in the mutant.
Q builds up, and far less R and S are made than in bacteria that lack the mutation.
S is made at the usual rate, as the cell makes a new enzyme because it needs S.
P builds up and no Q is made, as the whole pathway stops at its first step.

questions.stem: Why do phospholipids form a bilayer when they are mixed with water?

options.text: Enzymes in the cell join the phospholipids together into a sheet, using energy released from ATP.
The whole molecule repels water, so the phospholipids gather away from it as a droplet of oil.
Covalent bonds form between neighbouring phospholipids, linking them into one rigid sheet of molecules.
Hydrophilic heads face the water and hydrophobic tails are shielded from it, so the sheet forms spontaneously.

questions.explanation: In water the most stable arrangement is a continuous sheet two molecules thick, heads towards the water on both sides and tails in the middle. It forms with no energy input.

questions.stem: In bacteria, threonine is converted into isoleucine by a pathway of five enzyme-catalysed steps. What happens when isoleucine is added to a growing culture?

options.text: Isoleucine binds to the enzyme of the final step, the one that produced it, and blocks that single step only.
Isoleucine binds to an allosteric site on the first enzyme, reversibly reducing the pathway's activity.
The five enzymes are broken down, so the pathway cannot restart after the isoleucine is used up.
Isoleucine competes with threonine for the active site of the first enzyme, blocking it competitively.

questions.stem: Which statement about glycoproteins in the plasma membrane is correct?

options.text: Their carbohydrate is on the extracellular side and is used in cell recognition and adhesion.
Their carbohydrate is on the cytoplasmic side and is respired when the cell lacks glucose.
Their carbohydrate projects from both faces of the membrane so that either face can be recognised.
They are transport proteins whose carbohydrate forms the channel through which sugars enter the cell.

questions.explanation: Glycoproteins are proteins with a carbohydrate chain attached. The carbohydrate faces outwards, where it works in cell recognition and cell adhesion.

questions.stem: Methanol is not very toxic itself, but the enzyme alcohol dehydrogenase converts it into toxic products. Ethanol is also a substrate of alcohol dehydrogenase. Doctors have treated methanol poisoning by giving ethanol. Why does this reduce the harm?

options.text: Ethanol binds to an allosteric site, so the active site changes shape and methanol cannot bind.
Ethanol denatures alcohol dehydrogenase, so no methanol at all is converted.
Ethanol competes with methanol for the active site, so less methanol is converted at a time.
Ethanol binds to methanol molecules, so less methanol is free to reach the enzyme.

questions.stem: A student draws a two-dimensional representation of the fluid mosaic model. Which feature of the drawing is correct?

options.text: The tails of the inner layer point into the cytoplasm, as the cytoplasm is the inside of the cell.
The proteins are drawn at regular, equal spacings, like tiles set in a fixed pattern across the sheet.
Glycoproteins are drawn with their carbohydrate chains on the cytoplasmic side of the membrane.
Cholesterol is drawn among the phospholipids within the bilayer, not on its surface.

questions.explanation: Cholesterol sits within the bilayer among the phospholipids. The hydrophilic heads form both surfaces and the hydrophobic tails form the core.
